triage.name: Enlarged Prostate (BPH)
triage.reason: Older man with lower urinary tract symptoms; diagnosis reachable by history, exam including prostate exam, urinalysis and labs, with retention and prostate cancer as look-alikes.

demographics: Very common in men over 50; prevalence rises steadily with each decade of life
More common in men with obesity, type 2 diabetes, or heart disease

risk_factors.text: Family history of BPH or prostate surgery in a father or brother

family_history: Father or brother with BPH or prostate surgery

chief_complaints.text: I have to get up several times a night to pee
My stream is weak and it takes a while to get started
I feel like I can't empty my bladder all the way
I'm going to the bathroom all the time during the day
Sometimes I leak a little after I finish

hpi.onset: Gradual, over months to years; the patient often can't name a specific start
hpi.duration: Usually present for at least several months, often years, before the visit
hpi.progression: Slowly worsens over time; symptoms may fluctuate with fluid intake, alcohol, cold weather, or starting a new medication
hpi.location: Lower abdomen and pelvis; felt at the level of the bladder and urethra
hpi.radiation: No true radiation; discomfort may be felt as suprapubic fullness
hpi.quality: Obstructive symptoms (hesitancy, weak stream, straining, terminal dribbling) and irritative symptoms (frequency, urgency, nocturia) together
hpi.severity: Mild to moderate for most; a minority have severe symptoms that interfere with sleep and daily activities
hpi.timing: Nocturia is often the most bothersome; symptoms are worse at night and in cold weather

associated_symptoms.text: Nocturia (waking two or more times to urinate)

pertinent_negatives: Neurologic symptoms such as saddle numbness or leg weakness

atypical.how_it_differs: Symptoms may be attributed to normal aging or to other chronic conditions; nocturia and falls at night may be the main complaint rather than voiding symptoms.
missing_classic_features: Clear description of weak stream or hesitancy

atypical.how_it_differs: Coexisting diabetic neuropathy can cause a neurogenic bladder, so symptoms may reflect poor bladder contractility rather than obstruction alone.
Central adiposity and metabolic syndrome are associated with larger prostate volume and more rapid symptom progression.
Chronic obstruction can present with rising creatinine, anemia, or electrolyte abnormalities rather than bothersome voiding symptoms.

general.mild: Well-appearing older man, no distress, ambulates comfortably
general.moderate: Well-appearing but tired from nocturia; may shift in the chair or mention needing the bathroom
general.severe: Uncomfortable, restless, frequent trips to the bathroom; may appear sleep-deprived
general.critical: Ill-appearing and distressed with suprapubic pain and a visibly distended lower abdomen (acute retention)

findings.maneuver: Inspect and palpate the suprapubic area
findings.finding: Suprapubic fullness or a palpable bladder

findings.maneuver: Perform a digital rectal exam with the patient in the lateral decubitus or standing bent-over position, palpating the posterior surface of the prostate through the anterior rectal wall
findings.finding: Enlarged prostate with a smooth, rubbery, non-tender surface and preserved median sulcus

findings.maneuver: Perform a digital rectal exam, feeling for asymmetry, induration, or nodules
findings.finding: Hard, nodular, or asymmetric prostate with obliterated median sulcus

findings.maneuver: Assess anal sphincter tone during the digital rectal exam
Test sensation in the saddle distribution and check lower extremity strength and reflexes
findings.finding: Intact saddle sensation, normal strength and reflexes

findings.maneuver: Inspect the lower extremities for swelling
Auscultate the epigastrium and flanks for bruits

differential.name: Prostate cancer
differential.why_considered: Same age group, same lower urinary tract symptoms, and both can enlarge the prostate
differential.trigger: Hard, nodular, or asymmetric prostate on digital rectal exam, or bone pain or weight loss

history: Bone pain, especially back or hip
Unexplained weight loss
Family history of prostate cancer
exam: Hard, nodular, or asymmetric prostate with obliterated median sulcus
Palpable lymph nodes or focal bone tenderness
labs: Markedly elevated or rapidly rising PSA
Elevated alkaline phosphatase with bone involvement
imaging: Sclerotic bone lesions on bone scan or CT

differential.name: Acute urinary retention
differential.why_considered: The most feared acute consequence of an enlarged prostate; the patient cannot urinate at all
differential.trigger: Complete inability to urinate with a painful, distended bladder

history: Sudden inability to pass any urine
Severe suprapubic pain and urgency
Recent cold or allergy medicine, alcohol, or a long period of immobility
exam: Patient restless and in obvious distress
labs: Post-void residual near the full bladder capacity
imaging: Bladder ultrasound showing a large retained volume

differential.name: Urinary tract infection
differential.why_considered: Frequency, urgency, and nocturia overlap with BPH, and BPH predisposes to infection

history: Dysuria and foul-smelling or cloudy urine
Fever and chills
Symptoms came on over days rather than months

differential.name: Prostatitis
differential.why_considered: Causes urinary symptoms and pelvic pain in the same age group

history: Perineal or rectal pain
Pain with ejaculation
Acute onset, sometimes after a procedure or catheterization
exam: Firm, exquisitely tender prostate on digital rectal exam
labs: Elevated PSA that falls after treatment

differential.name: Neurogenic bladder
differential.why_considered: Poor bladder emptying with frequency and incomplete emptying can mimic obstruction

history: Known diabetes, stroke, Parkinson disease, or spinal cord disease
Fecal incontinence or saddle numbness
Symptoms of urgency and retention without a weak stream pattern
exam: Abnormal saddle sensation, anal sphincter tone, or lower extremity strength and reflexes
imaging: Urodynamic testing showing detrusor underactivity or overactivity rather than obstruction

differential.name: Urethral stricture
differential.why_considered: Obstructive voiding symptoms with a weak stream and straining

history: Prior urethral trauma, catheterization, or sexually transmitted infection
Younger age than typical BPH
exam: Normal or small prostate on digital rectal exam
Palpable urethral induration or a tight urethra on catheter passage
imaging: Narrowed urethral segment on retrograde urethrogram or cystoscopy

differential.name: Overactive bladder
differential.why_considered: Frequency, urgency, and nocturia are the dominant symptoms

history: Urgency with urge incontinence and little or no hesitancy or weak stream
Symptoms not worsened by cold medicines
exam: Normal prostate on digital rectal exam
imaging: Urodynamic testing showing detrusor overactivity without obstruction

differential.name: Bladder stone
differential.why_considered: Long-standing obstruction can cause stones that worsen voiding symptoms

history: Sudden interruption of the stream with severe pain
Pain radiating to the tip of the penis
imaging: Calcified opacity in the bladder on plain film, ultrasound, or CT

severity.mild: Mild symptoms that bother the patient little; nocturia once or twice, no significant interference with daily life; normal post-void residual and creatinine
severity.moderate: Bothersome frequency, urgency, weak stream, and nocturia that interfere with sleep and activities; post-void residual mildly elevated; creatinine normal
severity.severe: Marked obstructive symptoms with straining, incomplete emptying, and a palpable bladder; elevated post-void residual; may have rising creatinine or recurrent urinary tract infection
severity.critical: Acute urinary retention with a painful distended bladder, or obstructive uropathy with acute kidney injury and electrolyte disturbance

red_flags.finding: Complete inability to urinate with suprapubic pain and a distended bladder
red_flags.meaning: Acute urinary retention; needs immediate bladder decompression

red_flags.finding: Fever and chills with dysuria, frequency, and urgency
red_flags.meaning: Urinary tract infection or pyelonephritis; needs urgent treatment
Could be infection, stone, or urologic cancer; needs evaluation

red_flags.finding: Flank pain, rising creatinine, or decreased urine output
Hard, nodular, or asymmetric prostate on digital rectal exam
Saddle numbness, leg weakness, or fecal incontinence
red_flags.meaning: Cauda equina syndrome; a neurologic emergency

complications.name: Acute urinary retention
clues: Triggered by cold or allergy medicine, alcohol, cold weather, or immobility

complications.name: Urinary tract infection
clues: Dysuria, fever, cloudy or foul-smelling urine

complications.name: Bladder stones
clues: Pain radiating to the tip of the penis

complications.name: Recurrent urinary tract infections with urosepsis

special_populations.differences: Symptoms may be dismissed as normal aging; nocturia can lead to falls at night, and anticholinergic medicines for bladder symptoms can worsen retention and confusion.
Diabetic neuropathy can cause a neurogenic bladder, so poor emptying may reflect weak detrusor contractility rather than obstruction alone.
Central adiposity and metabolic syndrome are linked to larger prostate volume and faster symptom progression.
Chronic obstruction may present with rising creatinine, anemia, or electrolyte abnormalities rather than bothersome voiding symptoms.

key_questions.question: What urinary symptoms have you noticed — trouble starting, a weak or interrupted stream, straining, dribbling at the end?
key_questions.looking_for: Obstructive pattern: hesitancy, weak stream, straining, terminal dribbling

key_questions.question: How many times do you get up at night to urinate?
key_questions.looking_for: Nocturia two or more times; often the most bothersome symptom

key_questions.question: How often are you urinating during the day, and do you get sudden urges?
Do you feel like your bladder is not completely empty after you finish?
key_questions.looking_for: Sensation of incomplete emptying; suggests significant residual volume

key_questions.question: How long has this been going on, and is it getting worse?
key_questions.looking_for: Gradual onset over months to years, slowly progressive

key_questions.question: What makes it worse — cold weather, alcohol, caffeine, cold or allergy medicines, fluids before bed?
key_questions.looking_for: Worsening with decongestants or antihistamines, alcohol, caffeine, evening fluids

key_questions.question: Have you ever been completely unable to urinate?
key_questions.looking_for: Any episode of acute urinary retention; a urologic emergency

key_questions.question: Have you seen blood in your urine?
key_questions.looking_for: Gross hematuria — needs evaluation for infection, stone, or urologic cancer

key_questions.question: Any fever, chills, burning with urination, or cloudy or foul-smelling urine?
key_questions.looking_for: Urinary tract infection; BPH predisposes to it

key_questions.question: Any pain in your back or flanks, or pain with ejaculation?
key_questions.looking_for: Flank pain suggests obstruction or pyelonephritis; ejaculatory pain suggests prostatitis

key_questions.question: Have you had any unexplained weight loss or bone pain, especially in your back or hips?
key_questions.looking_for: Features suggesting prostate cancer with bone involvement

key_questions.question: What medicines do you take, including over-the-counter cold, allergy, or sleep aids?
key_questions.looking_for: Anticholinergics, antihistamines, decongestants, and diuretics that worsen voiding

key_questions.question: Has a father or brother had an enlarged prostate, prostate surgery, or prostate cancer?
key_questions.looking_for: Family history of BPH or prostate surgery

key_questions.question: Do you have diabetes, heart disease, or problems with your weight or activity level?
key_questions.looking_for: Obesity, type 2 diabetes, heart disease — associated with larger prostate and faster progression

key_questions.question: Any numbness in the saddle area, leg weakness, or trouble controlling your bowels?
key_questions.looking_for: Cauda equina syndrome — a neurologic emergency

key_questions.question: How much alcohol and caffeine do you drink, and how much fluid do you take in the evening?
key_questions.looking_for: Modifiable triggers of nocturia and urgency

key_questions.question: Any changes in erections or sexual function?
key_questions.looking_for: Erectile dysfunction, which is associated with BPH and affects treatment choice

reasoning_points: Older man with a gradual, months-to-years history of lower urinary tract symptoms
Both obstructive symptoms (hesitancy, weak stream, straining, terminal dribbling) and irritative symptoms (frequency, urgency, nocturia)
Nocturia is often the most bothersome complaint
Symptoms fluctuate with cold weather, alcohol, caffeine, and cold or allergy medicines
Digital rectal exam shows an enlarged, smooth, rubbery, non-tender prostate with a preserved median sulcus
No fever, dysuria, gross hematuria, flank pain, or bone pain to suggest infection, stone, or cancer
Urinalysis is negative for infection and blood; creatinine is normal
Post-void residual and prostate size support obstruction rather than a primary bladder problem

easy: Classic gradual nocturia, frequency, weak stream, and hesitancy
Enlarged smooth prostate on digital rectal exam
medium: Symptoms attributed to normal aging or to another chronic condition
Coexisting overactive bladder with urgency and urge incontinence
Mild pyuria or a borderline PSA that needs interpretation
Patient on an anticholinergic or decongestant that is worsening symptoms
hard: Older adult whose main complaint is falls at night from nocturia rather than voiding symptoms
Man with diabetes and a neurogenic bladder that mimics obstruction
Presentation with rising creatinine and obstructive uropathy but few urinary complaints
Acute urinary retention triggered by a cold medicine or alcohol
Hard, nodular prostate on exam raising concern for prostate cancer
